statement: In some countries, fewer young people are visiting museums and art galleries than in the past.
question: Why is this the case? What can museums and galleries do to attract more young visitors?
model:
For many teenagers, a museum is associated with compulsory school trips and long corridors of glass cases. It is therefore unsurprising that visitor numbers among young people have fallen in some countries, although institutions that are willing to adapt can certainly reverse this trend.

One reason for the decline is the overwhelming competition for young people's leisure time. Streaming services, video games and social media offer instant, personalised entertainment at home, and by comparison a gallery in which visitors are expected to walk quietly and read lengthy labels can seem dull and demanding. Another factor is that much of what museums display is now available online: a student can view high-resolution images of the Mona Lisa without queuing behind hundreds of tourists. Cost can also be a barrier, since many special exhibitions charge entrance fees that are beyond the means of students. Finally, some young people feel that museums are formal, intimidating places intended for older, more educated visitors, and that their own interests and backgrounds are not reflected in the collections.

Museums can respond in several ways. Firstly, they can make visits more interactive and social. Late-night openings with music, food and talks, such as those held at many London museums, have proved remarkably popular with people in their twenties. Secondly, they can embrace digital technology rather than compete with it, using augmented reality to bring dinosaur skeletons to life or inviting visitors to share content online. Offering free or heavily discounted entry for under-25s would remove the financial obstacle. Most importantly, involving young people in planning exhibitions, perhaps through youth panels, would ensure that displays address issues they genuinely care about.

In conclusion, young people are visiting museums less because of digital competition, cost and a perception that these institutions are not for them. By becoming more interactive, affordable and inclusive, museums can win back this crucial audience.
